title: Notification system requirements
idea: Scoping a notification system means naming who sends what to whom, on which channel, how urgent it is, and which delivery guarantee you promise.
points: Other services ask it to notify a user by email, SMS or push.
Each message comes from a stored template filled with per-user values.
Each channel lists backup providers, so one vendor outage need not stop delivery.
Assume OTPs in seconds, promotions later; a caller's retry never creates a second notification.

hero.title: Actors and use cases in v1

edges.caption: A calling service sends a request with a user id, a notification type and template values.
The system checks whether the user allows this type on this channel.
Allowed requests get their template rendered into a subject and a body.
A provider for the channel sends it. A failing provider hands over to the next one.
Callers can ask what happened: sent, failed, or skipped because of an opt-out.

edges.label: sets
edges.caption: The end user is an actor too: their opt-outs decide what is allowed.
Weekly digests, an in-app inbox and campaign scheduling wait for later. Say so out loud.

code.title: Notification types as an enum
code.caption: The scope as code: each notification type carries its priority, whether users may opt out, and its channels.

walk.text: v1 is a named set of types. Anything missing is out of scope.
Print every type with its scope, priority, opt-out rule and channels.
Three channels and three priority levels, fixed for v1.
OTP is critical and cannot be muted; promotions are low priority and can.
Digests and the inbox are listed as OUT, so the cut is visible.

pitfalls: Do not promise exactly-once delivery; providers can deliver twice after a timeout.
Never let users opt out of security messages such as OTPs.
State volume and latency as assumptions, like "OTP within seconds", not as facts.

quiz.q: A login OTP must arrive fast. Which scoping decision fits best?
options: Send it through the same queue as promotions
Give it its own high-priority path and allow no opt-out
Let the user mute it like any other message
Batch it into the weekly digest
quiz.why: An OTP is useless if it waits behind bulk mail. A separate priority keeps it fast, and muting it would lock users out.

takeaway: Name the types, channels, priorities and the dedupe-by-key rule first.
